headline: Meta Ordered To Pay New Mexico $25 Billion For Deceiving Facebook Users About Privacy
standfirst: A judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in civil penalties for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook.
body_markdown:
A judge in New Mexico has ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in civil penalties for deceiving users about privacy on Facebook. The ruling Wednesday by state District Court Judge Francis J. Mathew came in the state’s landmark Cambridge Analytica case against Facebook for violations of New Mexico’s Unfair Practices Act. (Deadline)

**Axios** adds: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion in penalties Wednesday after a jury found in September that the social media giant misled users about their data privacy. Why it matters: The penalties come nearly a decade after the Cambridge Analytica scandal first broke and signal that Big Tech can face significant financial consequences for misleading users about their privacy.

**BBC News US & Canada** adds: The fine is the largest to date against Facebook's owner, larger than an $18bn deal with California.

**MyJoyOnline** adds: Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, has been hit with the largest ever fine against it for its business practices. A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data.

**France 24** adds: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion after a jury found the company deceived users in a case linked to the Cambridge Analytica scandal, media reported Wednesday. The ruling follows an $18 billion settlement with 48 other states over similar claims.

This digest was assembled automatically from reporting by Deadline, MyJoyOnline, ABC News Australia, The Japan Times, The Straits Times, BBC News US & Canada, Los Angeles Times, France 24 and Axios. Follow the source links below for the full coverage.
